info.title: TorqueLane API
info.description: TorqueLane API. Errors always use the envelope { "error": { "code", "message", "details"? } }; clients branch on `code`. Records outside the tenant scope of the caller answer 404 not_found, exactly like records that do not exist.

servers.description: Relative to the environment host, e.g. https://api-staging.<domain>

get.description:
Most severe first, then most urgent. PMS alerts only where repair_pms
is active. Ids are deterministic (`pms:<vehicle>:<task>`,
`doc:<document>`, `licence:<vehicle>`, …). `?include_dismissed=1` adds
dismissed ones (flagged).

The fleet overview in one call: the fleet summary, overdue and
due-soon demand (`serviceDemand`), 30-day rolling spend, twelve months
of closed cost, the six-week upcoming load, stale odometers, expiring
documents, the three most urgent items, and the next five active work
orders by scheduled date.

Every tracked interval across the fleet, most urgent first
(`compareUrgency`), grouped by lead time: overdue, next 7, next 30 and
next 90 days (each with its catalogue cost). `status` (ok | due_soon |
overdue) filters the rows; the six-week load and the demand bands are
always the whole fleet's, the same figures the dashboard shows.

Over the last `months` (3, 6 or 12; default 12) of closed work: monthly
cost and maintenance mix, total and preventive share of spend, cost per
fleet kilometre (distance driven IN the period, from each vehicle's
daily average), mean days between services, and the rankings: costliest
vehicles, spend by service item, services per 10,000 km.

cost_per_km_cents.description: Centavos per km driven in the period, rounded once (half up).

get.description:
What "Auto-schedule overdue" would book: every overdue item no live
work order covers, worst first, from tomorrow at three a day (critical
tasks as critical, the rest high), each with its estimate (catalogue
parts + hours at the shop rate), and the total. Accounts that take no
new work are left out. `POST /work-orders/auto-schedule` books exactly
this, recomputed. `can_commit`: the caller holds `workorder:create`.

The approvals queue (../web's Requests screen): quotations pending
approval, oldest first, each with its pending value, business hours
waited against its own SLA, and whether the caller may decide it; what
waits on the caller; approved work not yet booked; spend committed
this Manila month against the scope's monthly budget; and the mean
approval turnaround. Every order is judged against its OWN effective
settings. Staff may narrow to one `customer_account_id`. Needs
repair_pms.

Staff. The organization's defaults, the selected branch's override
(X-Branch-Id) and what that branch runs on.

put.description: `settings:manage` in that branch. A null field inherits the organization's.

get.description:
The account's sparse overrides and the settings they resolve to (for
staff, in the selected branch). Anyone who can see the account; a
portal user's own.

post.description: `settings:manage` and access to `branch_id`.

delete.description: A technician's home bay is a 409.

post.description: Needs `organization:manage`. Every module starts switched off.

put.description: Needs `settings:manage` and access to the branch.

delete.description:
Needs `organization:manage`. A branch with bays, technicians, pinned
staff or document series is a 409: mark it inactive instead.

get.description:
Exact match on the normalised plate (case, spaces, dashes ignored), then
the VIN, over the vehicles the caller may see. Under 3 characters the
outcome is `idle`; no match is `new` (a 17-character entry is taken as
a VIN). A stale odometer is never pre-filled: `form.odometer` is null
and `form.odometer_needs_confirmation` true, with the last reading in
`last_odometer` for reference.
get.summary: Look up a vehicle by plate or VIN

post.description:
Staff with `customer:manage` and `vehicle:manage`. One transaction:
the account with its opening consents (service records must be
granted), and the vehicle with the reading taken at the counter.
post.summary: Register a new customer and vehicle at the counter

get.description: Every decision, newest first (cursor-paginated).

post.description:
`customer:manage`. Staff record how the customer told them (in person,
paper form, email, SMS, phone); a portal user records their own through
the `portal` channel. Allowed on a suspended account.

get.description: The latest decision per purpose, for the account and for each contact.

post.description: `customer:manage`. Marking one primary demotes the previous primary.

delete.description: A contact with consent decisions on record cannot be deleted (409).

get.summary: Return an empty response simply to trigger the storage of the CSRF cookie in the browser

post.description:
Staff with `customer:manage`. `consents` must include `service_records`,
granted; it is recorded in the same transaction as the account.

put.description:
`customer:manage`. Portal users may edit only their own account's
contact details and branding.

post.description:
Staff with `settings:manage`. The account's portal users are locked out
at once and it takes no new work; staff can still read it.
Staff with `settings:manage`.

get.description:
One customer account's projected spare-parts demand over
`horizon_weeks` (default 6; ../web `computePartsDemand`): its vehicles'
PMS items falling due, less what live work orders and open purchase
orders already cover, against the account's own stock. Rows rank by
shortfall, then quantity required. `summary` is the frontend's
sentence; `can_raise` says whether the caller may turn rows into
purchase requests (`po:issue`, and the account takes new work). Needs
repair_pms.

The documents screen's tiles under the list's filters: how many, their
total size in bytes, and how many expire within the 45-day warning
window (already expired included).

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: The expiry badge: expired, expiring (within 30 days) or ok.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Name, notes, uploader or plate, case-insensitive.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: uploaded (newest first, the default) or expiry (soonest first, undated last).

get.description:
Newest upload first, or `sort=expiry` (soonest first, undated last).
Filter by `vehicle_id`, `customer_account_id`, `kind`,
`expiring_within` days, expiry `status` (expired, expiring within 30
days, ok) and `q` (name, notes, uploader, plate).

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: The expiry badge: expired, expiring (within 30 days) or ok.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Name, notes, uploader or plate, case-insensitive.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: uploaded (newest first, the default) or expiry (soonest first, undated last).

post.description:
`document:upload`, multipart. With `vehicle_id` the document is filed
under the vehicle's current owner; otherwise under `customer_account_id`.
Only renewal kinds (registration, CTPL, comprehensive insurance,
emission test, LTFRB franchise, warranty) take `expires_on`. Up to
10 MB of PDF, JPEG, PNG, WebP or HEIC.

delete.description: `document:delete`. The file is removed after the row's deletion commits.

get.description:
A short-lived (60 s) URL to the file, issued after the policy check.
409 for a record with no file (imported paper records).

Streams a document's file. Reachable only through the signed, 60-second
URL from GET /documents/{id}/download: the signature (bound to the
document id and expiry, checked by the `signed` middleware) is the
credential, so there is no session and the lookup runs in the named
system context "signed document download".

Portal users see their account's parts; staff every account's (narrow
with `customer_account_id`). Active parts only unless
`include_inactive`. Needs repair_pms.

post.description:
`settings:manage`. Staff name the `customer_account_id`; a portal
user's part goes to their own account. `current_stock` is the opening
count; afterwards stock changes only by receiving a purchase order.

put.description:
`settings:manage`. Stock and account cannot change here. `usages`, when
sent, replaces the part's task links.

delete.description:
Only a part never ordered; one on a purchase order answers 409 (set
`is_active: false` instead).

get.description:
The dashboard KPIs over the caller's vehicles (staff may narrow to one
`customer_account_id`), the expiring-documents tile and the thresholds
behind them. Needs repair_pms.

Database and queue status, for uptime monitors. `degraded` (queue
heartbeat missing or older than five minutes) still answers 200; an
unreachable database answers 503 in the error envelope, with the report
under `details.health`.

message.const: The API cannot reach its database.

get.description: `access:manage`.

post.description:
`access:manage`. Portal roles must name an active `customer_account_id`;
staff roles must not name one. You can only invite to roles whose grants
you hold, and a branch-pinned manager only into their own branches.
The invitation link is emailed; the token is never returned.

Creates the account from the emailed invitation token and signs the new
user in (when called with a cookie session). Answers with the same body
as `GET /me`. Rate-limited.

get.description: Every row, newest first, void rows included.

post.description:
`vehicle:update`. Refused below the current reading (422, the
frontend's message). A reading implying over 3× or under 0.1× the
vehicle's average daily distance is a 422 warning on `value` until
re-sent with `confirm_warning: true`. Not in the future, not dated
before the current reading.

`vehicle:manage`. Appends a correction row; nothing is edited or
deleted. A vehicle keeps at least one effective reading.

get.description:
Every module with its organization switch and, per branch the caller can
reach, the branch switch and whether it is active there. Staff only.

put.description:
Needs `organization:manage`. Switching it off turns it off in every
branch at once.
put.summary: Switch a module for the organization

put.description:
Needs `settings:manage` and access to the branch. Has no effect while
the organization switch is off.
put.summary: Switch a module for a branch

post.description:
Emails a reset link when the address belongs to an account. Answers the
same either way, so it cannot be used to discover accounts.
Rate-limited.
Uses the token from the reset email. Rate-limited.

patch.description:
First name, last name (the display `name` becomes "first last") and a
username (letters, digits, `.`, `-`, `_`; unique in the organization,
case-insensitively; 422 when taken). Answers the refreshed session.

get.description:
The signed-in user, their organization, side, branches (allowed and
selected), customer account (portal), resolved capabilities, active
modules and branding. The frontend gates its UI from this.

put.description:
`current_password` must match (422 otherwise); the new `password`
(with `password_confirmation`) needs 8+ characters and must differ.
Other devices' sessions and remember-me cookies stop working; this
session stays signed in.

get.description:
Newest first. Portal users see their account's; staff every account's
(narrow with `customer_account_id`); filter by `status`. Needs
repair_pms.

post.description:
`po:issue`. Name the parts to order (`part_ids`) over the horizon the
forecast was read at; the server recomputes the forecast and orders
each part's shortfall at its unit cost, one draft per preferred
vendor. Quantities and prices are never read from the request. A
suspended account takes no new orders (403 account_suspended).
post.summary: Raise purchase requests from the forecast

get.description:
The list's filters as a spreadsheet (`format` xlsx, the default, or
csv): one row per line, ../web `exportPurchaseOrdersToExcel`. Money as
pesos with two decimals. At most 5,000 orders; filter to narrow.

One order, one row per line (../web `exportPurchaseOrderToExcel`),
named after its reference.

post.description:
draft → sent. `po:issue`, and the order's total must sit within the
caller's approval band under the account's settings (403 otherwise,
naming the limit).

sent → received. Each line's quantity goes back into the account's own
stock of that part.
draft or sent → cancelled, with a `reason`. Its number is not reused.

get.description: In catalogue order (ties in urgency keep it), inactive ones included.

post.description: Staff with `settings:manage`.

put.description:
Editing an interval never changes any vehicle's recorded service
history; due dates move because they are derived.

delete.description: Only one no vehicle has history for (409 otherwise; deactivate it).

post.description:
Cookie-session login for the SPA: call `GET /sanctum/csrf-cookie` first,
then post with the `X-XSRF-TOKEN` header, from an allowed origin. Answers
with the same body as `GET /me`. A session that would resolve to no
tenant scope (a suspended account's portal user, a disabled user) is
refused with its reason. Rate-limited per email and per IP.

Ends the cookie session. Works for any signed-in user, including one
whose account was suspended mid-session.

get.description: Approved or scheduled work booked for `date` (default today).
On the floor now, longest-running first, with minutes elapsed since start.
Closed, not yet collected: outstanding, oldest completion first.

Quotations waiting on the customer, longest wait first, in business
hours (Mon–Fri 08:00–18:00 Manila), against each order's SLA.

Booked hours per bay on `date` (catalogue estimates, else labour at
the shop rate, else an hour) against capacity; nothing stops a bay
reading over 100%. `days` adds a trailing daily utilisation series.

Per technician: the job in hand, jobs closed in [`from`, `to`), and mean
actual hours (start → close event) against the estimate.

Recognised on collection, in [`from`, `to`) (default: this month to
date), by customer account and by service item.

The shop home in one call: arriving today, on the floor (elapsed
against the estimate), quotes waiting on the customer (oldest first,
the longest wait in business hours), ready for collection (with the
value on the lot), bay utilisation today, and revenue this week
(Monday start, Manila) against last week. Each order carries its
vehicle and customer name.

value_cents.description: The estimate's labour + parts of every finished job still on the lot.

get.description:
Over the last `months` (3, 6 or 12; default 6), recognised on
collection: revenue by customer and by service item (top 10), approval
turnaround by customer, the maintenance mix by month, and the parts
margin on closed work; plus 21 days of bay utilisation.

Every customer account the shop looks after, biggest spender this
month first: vehicles, open work, mean approval turnaround, revenue
recognised this month (to now), and closed work not yet collected. An
order counts for the account stamped on it at creation.

One customer account from the shop's side: its rollup, its vehicles
(with PMS health where repair_pms is on), its work-order history
(latest first), and its terms: the account, its sparse approval
overrides, and the settings they resolve to.

post.description: `settings:manage` and access to `branch_id`.

put.description:
`access:manage`. Not yourself, and never to or from a role whose grants
you do not hold. `branch_ids: []` means every branch, which only an
unrestricted manager can grant. Roles never move between staff and
portal.

get.description:
`q` matches a plate or VIN on its normalised form ("abc-1234" finds
"ABC 1234"), exactly or as a plate prefix; `search` is a substring of
plate, make, model, driver or location. Filter by `status`,
`customer_account_id`, `department`, and `pms` (ok, due_soon, overdue:
the worst band; stale: odometer over 14 days old). `sort=health` lists
the least healthy first (else by plate).

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Plate or VIN, matched on the normalised form (check-in style).

parameters.name: pms
parameters.description: Derived, so evaluated per request: the worst PMS band, or an odometer reading over 14 days old.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Plate, make, model, driver or location, case-insensitive substring.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: plate (the default) or health (least healthy first).

post.description:
`vehicle:manage`. Staff name the `customer_account_id`; a portal user
registers to their own account. Takes the first odometer reading and
any known service history. A suspended account takes no new vehicles
(403 account_suspended).

put.description:
`vehicle:manage`. Never the odometer (POST …/readings) or the owner
(POST …/transfer).

delete.description:
`vehicle:manage`. Vehicles are never deleted: history stays and the
plate becomes free for another vehicle.

post.description:
Staff with `vehicle:manage`. Service history (readings, maintenance
state) stays with the vehicle; documents stay with the account they
were filed under, so the new owner never sees the previous owner's.
The receiving account must be active.

get.description: Staff only (it names other customer accounts).

Every catalogue task evaluated against the vehicle, most urgent first,
with the health score (steep: overdue critical −25, overdue −15,
due-soon critical −8, due-soon −4). Needs repair_pms.
By name.

post.description: `settings:manage`. Names are unique in the organization.

delete.description: Past work orders keep the vendor's name.

get.description:
Portal users see their account's orders; staff see the organization's,
limited to their branches (a portal request not yet taken into a branch
is visible to all staff). Filter with `status[]`, `stage` (active,
completed, cancelled), `type`, `q` (reference, title, technician,
vendor, plate, customer), `customer_account_id`, `vehicle_id`, `branch_id`,
`technician_id`, `bay_id`, `scheduled_for`; order with `sort` (opened,
the default; scheduled; completed; queue).

post.description:
`workorder:create`. Starts as an unnumbered draft — the number is issued
when it is sent for approval. Lines carry quantities and rates; the
server prices them (any cost or total sent is ignored). Staff raise it
in a branch (`branch_id`, else X-Branch-Id, else their only branch); a
suspended account takes no new work (403 account_suspended).

get.description:
What the list screens total, under the same filters as the list:
orders per bucket (active, completed, cancelled, all) within the scope
filters (`customer_account_id`, `vehicle_id`, `branch_id`), and the
count and value in centavos (labour plus resolved parts) of the fully
filtered set.

post.description:
The check-out panel's "Mark collected": every order in `work_order_ids`
must be closed and not yet collected (409 invalid_transition
otherwise, and none is collected). Staff with `workorder:complete`.

`workorder:create`. Raises one draft per proposal in
`GET /analytics/auto-schedule` (recomputed here, so an item already
covered is never booked twice): the catalogue task as its one line,
scheduled from tomorrow at three a day. Staff narrow with
`customer_account_id` and name the `branch_id` taking the work in (else
X-Branch-Id, else their only repair branch).

patch.description:
`workorder:update`. A declined quote reopens as a draft (it keeps its
number). Any other status is 409.

put.description:
`workorder:update`. The full list: lines with an `id` are updated, new
ones created, missing ones removed. Every cost is recomputed from
quantity × rate on the server.

post.description:
`workorder:update`. Issues the order number. Under the account's
auto-approve ceiling the system approves every line and the order opens
as approved.

`workorder:approve`, within the role's approval band for the pending
amount. Declining a safety-critical line needs a `note`. The order's
status follows from the lines.

Staff, `workorder:update`. Approved work gets a date, a time and a bay
(and optionally a technician); a scheduled order may be re-booked.

`workorder:complete`, while in progress: findings, odometer at service,
parts fitted, tasks discharged.

`workorder:complete`. Refused (409, `details.reason` variance_exceeded)
when actual cost passes the approved amount by more than the variance
threshold, unless `variance_approved` is sent by someone who can
approve the actual amount. Closing resets the vehicle's PMS intervals.

CheckInRequest.description:
GET /check-in/lookup?q=… and POST /check-in (a new customer and vehicle at
the counter).
CheckInRequest.title: CheckInRequest

ConsentChannel.description:
How a consent decision reached us. | | |---| | `in_person`
| | `paper_form`
| | `email`
| | `sms`
| | `phone`
| | `portal`
| | `import`
Carried over from a record that predates the ledger (the demo seed). |
ConsentChannel.title: ConsentChannel

ConsentPurpose.description: What a customer agreed to (Data Privacy Act, RA 10173). `service_records` is the floor: without it the shop cannot keep a job history at all, so an account cannot be created without it granted.
ConsentPurpose.title: ConsentPurpose

captured_by.description: Which staff member recorded it is the shop's business, not the customer's.

note.description: Required to decline safety-critical work (checked against the line).

DocumentKind.description: Port of ../web's `DocumentKind` and lib/documents.ts / lib/compliance.ts kind sets. Labels are verbatim: alert bodies and the expiring-documents tile print them.
DocumentKind.title: DocumentKind

needs_reorder.description: At or below its reorder point.

LineUrgency.description: A safety-critical line cannot be declined without a reason on record.
LineUrgency.title: LineUrgency

selected.description: One branch id, "all" (staff across every allowed branch), or null (portal).

recorded_by.description: Which staff member recorded it is the shop's business.

PartsSource.description: Who supplies a line's part: the shop buys it in (and earns its markup), or it comes from the customer's own stock (no margin).
PartsSource.title: PartsSource

RaisePurchaseOrdersRequest.description:
Purchase requests from the forecast: the parts chosen, over the horizon the
forecast was read at. Quantities and prices come from the server's own
forecast, never from here.
RaisePurchaseOrdersRequest.title: RaisePurchaseOrdersRequest

confirm_warning.description: Required to save a reading the validation flags as unusual.

Role.description: Every role a user can hold. The eight ported roles keep the frontend's values, labels and descriptions (golden-tested against rbac.json). `branch_manager` and `cashier` are staff roles new in the API. "Owner" is not a separate role: the owner is a `provider_admin`.
Role.title: Role

SaveAccountApprovalSettingsRequest.description:
The account's sparse approval overrides: a key sets that band, null goes
back to inheriting, an absent key is unchanged. Money in centavos.
SaveAccountApprovalSettingsRequest.title: SaveAccountApprovalSettingsRequest

SaveApprovalSettingsRequest.description:
PUT /approval-settings (organization defaults) and
PUT /branches/{branch}/approval-settings (a branch's sparse override; null
clears a field back to inheriting). Money in centavos.

vat_rate_pct.description: 0 is a real rate (not VAT-registered), not a missing one.

SaveApprovalSettingsRequest.title: SaveApprovalSettingsRequest

SaveCustomerAccountRequest.description:
POST creates (with opening consents), PATCH edits. Status changes have their
own endpoints, and the account type never changes. Portal users may edit
their own account's contact details and branding, not the shop's commercial
or internal fields.
SaveCustomerAccountRequest.title: SaveCustomerAccountRequest

SaveFleetPartRequest.description:
A customer's spare part. `customer_account_id` (staff; a portal user's own
account otherwise) and `current_stock` are accepted on create only: after
that, stock changes by receiving purchase orders. `usages` replaces the
part's task links when given.
SaveFleetPartRequest.title: SaveFleetPartRequest

SaveVehicleRequest.description:
POST registers a vehicle with its first odometer reading (and any known
service history); PATCH edits details. The odometer never changes here
(POST …/readings), nor the owner (POST …/transfer).
SaveVehicleRequest.title: SaveVehicleRequest

SaveWorkOrderRequest.description:
POST /work-orders (createDraft) and PATCH /work-orders/{id} (updateDraft).
Lines are set on creation here, afterwards through PUT …/lines.
SaveWorkOrderRequest.title: SaveWorkOrderRequest

customer_account_id.description: Required for portal roles, forbidden for staff ones (decided by the role, in CreateInvitation).

username.description: Letters, digits, dot, dash, underscore; 3–32 characters.

branch_ids.description: [] = every branch (only an unrestricted granter may give that).

UploadDocumentRequest.description:
multipart/form-data: `file` plus metadata. Name a `vehicle_id` (the
document is filed under the vehicle's current owner) or a
`customer_account_id` (an account-level document).

work_order_id.description: Attach to a work order: filed under the order's account, on its vehicle.

UploadDocumentRequest.title: UploadDocumentRequest

stale.description: Older than the stale threshold: re-read the dash, don't trust it.

km_remaining.description: For the list's progress meter: km left (negative = past) and the interval used.

WorkOrderLinesRequest.description: PUT /work-orders/{id}/lines (recordLines): the draft's full line list.
WorkOrderLinesRequest.title: WorkOrderLinesRequest

waiting_hours.description: While pending: business hours waited so far, and whether that is past the SLA.

can_approve.description:
Whether the caller may decide the pending lines: the capability and
authority over the order's pending value (DecideLines checks both again).

WorkOrderStepRequest.description:
The bodies of the lifecycle steps: schedule, start, complete, close,
cancel. Each route uses the rules for its own step (route name suffix).
WorkOrderStepRequest.title: WorkOrderStepRequest

Error.conflict.description: The request conflicts with the current state.
